verdict.rationale: Inngest's own functions run automatically in response to events. The docs say events trigger function starts, runs can be triggered by other runs via events, and webhook URLs ingest third-party events; a user also describes it as a trigger solution. Declarative 'rules', meaning conditional filters or expressions that decide when an event fires an action, are not documented, and event-trigger configuration itself is shown only indirectly. missing for 10: explicit documentation of defining event triggers on functions, conditional rule/filter expressions on events, no-code or AI-native rule authoring, independent hands-on corroboration of rule-based triggering.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Events that exceed the rate limit are skipped and do not trigger functions to start.
Any run triggered by another run (via event, invoke, or defer) inherits its parent's sessions.
Inngest enables you to create any number of unique URLs which act as webhook consumers.
We needed a scheduling, queue, trigger solution.
